title: Launcher save(): handle a Windows sharing violation on the atomic results replace instead of killing the run
outcome: Consolidated Claude reviewer hypothesis, NOT a reproduced defect: periodic Rust reads of results.json may collide with Node renameSync replacement on Windows and cause sharing violations. Inspect actual open/share flags and deployed Node behavior; use a disposable focused deterministic reader/writer or stress check with original exit/error evidence. Do not touch live run artifacts, add speculative retries, or classify as confirmed without reproduction. If proven, propose bounded sharing-violation handling preserving atomic-reader and terminal-evidence guarantees; otherwise document measured scope and close only with owner approval. Source anchors scripts/test-launcher.mjs:50, src/test_runs_disk.rs read path. Parent full gate passed; this investigation was not run by reviewers or coordinator.
acceptance: Fail-first: a deterministic test holds the target open from another process during save() and shows the unchanged save() throws EPERM. The failed run is kept and cited.

save() handles a sharing violation on the rename only. On Windows, an EPERM, EACCES or EBUSY from the rename retries the same rename with a short backoff up to a stated bound, then throws the original error. The temp write is unchanged and completes before the first rename. Each reader sees either the previous complete file or the new one, never a partial one. A target released within the bound is replaced; one held past the bound fails with the original error, keeps its previous complete content, and leaves no temp file behind.
No test, stage or launcher-level retry is added. Any other error is thrown at once, as today. Terminal results still go through the same save(), so terminal evidence is never lost to a silent retry.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree; its run directory and fingerprint are cited in a note.
